sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Flow cytometry with the N-terminal Myc tag confirmed robust surface expression of the full-length tagged construct; truncation variants (p.Gln270*, p.Pro478Hisfs*18, p.Tyr660Serfs*16) lost surface signal, validating the assay. OSM-driven signaling function of the tagged construct was NOT MEASURED.
sites.rationale: The paper explicitly names the junction as between residues 27 and 28, which is confirmed by the topology landmarks: residue 27 (A) is the last signal-peptide residue and residue 28 (E) is the first extracellular residue of the mature protein. Python lookup confirms residue_before=A, residue_after=E. The tag is placed at the mature N-terminus, 712 residues from the TM boundary (TM starts at 740), satisfying all distance and extracellular constraints. This is the canonical position for an N-terminal epitope tag on a type I single-pass receptor. Full-length human OSMRβ expressed in mammalian cells with a Myc tag inserted between residues 27 and 28 (immediately downstream of the signal peptide cleavage site), generating an N-terminally Myc-tagged mature OSMRβ protein used to assess surface versus intracellular localization by flow cytometry.

sources.claim: A Myc tag was inserted between residues 27 and 28, immediately downstream of the signal peptide cleavage site ( 36 ), thereby generating an N-terminally Myc-tagged mature OSMRβ protein.

literature_notes: L2 corroborates the surface-display assay established by L1 and additionally mentions a C-terminal GFP tag on OSMRβ. The C-terminal end of OSMRβ (residue 979) falls within the intracellular domain (761–979), so the C-terminal GFP is not a surface tag site and is recorded in other_positions. No other ledger lines ground additional extracellular insertion sites.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal GFP tag on full-length OSMRβ; the C-terminus (residue 979) is intracellular (domain 761–979), so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not accessible on the cell surface.
